Texas Countdown, a weekly report on what's up in aerospace.

Senator William Blakely sold his 34% interest in Braniff Airways Friday to four top executives of Texas Instruments.
The deal amounted to about $13.5 million.
The buyers were J. Eric Johnson, TI board chairman, Eugene McDermott, Cecil Green, and P.E. Haggerty.
They stressed, however, that the buy was in the nature of personal investments
and that the purchase had no connection with Texas Instruments.
In space news, the mastermind of the Soviet space program resigned this week.
He is Alexander Nezmayanov, who, it's speculated, was relieved of his job
because of a new Kremlin program to speed up the conversion of research results into practical application.
Meanwhile, it was announced at the same time that several of Russia's top air force and
military men died in a so-called aviation catastrophe.
No details were given.

could tell us if Commander Alan Shepard's flight had any valid scientific value to it?
Yes, there is no question that it has had a very great value, because during all this
this time when he was in a very good state, this flight was a true base flight or let's say cosmic flight in every respect.
I wonder if you can tell us if you believe that Yuri Gagarin, the so-called Russian cosmonaut,
if Yuri Gagarin's flight was actually true or do you think it was a hoax? Can you comment on that?
I was not there, but for this reason I cannot say that it took place. But if you cannot prove the contrary, you have to accept it.
Do you think the publicity given our space flight, that is with Commander Shepard, was a good thing, or do you think we should have announced it after the fact?
Since it was successful, I think it was very good and it has a tremendous effect all over
the world.
Have you received any communications from Germany or Europe on that fact, for example
television coverage and so forth?
Yes, I got letters and they were all very pleased that it had been done and that it
was successful.

picked up something in space that they said sounded like two men and a woman.

President Kennedy told representatives of missile-based labor unions and contractors Tuesday
that the nation's security is tied to their efforts.
In effect, he told them to get on the ball and cut out the strikes
that cripple this country's missile and space efforts.
In this same connection, a report circulated by the Commerce Department indicated that Russia may enjoy a bigger space power lead over us than we thought.
It suggests that the Soviets already have a rocket more powerful than our giant Saturn rocket still on the drawing board.

Meantime, this announcement from Washington this week,
the administration is planning a major change in the National Space Program
by giving the Air Force responsibility for developing a new family of huge launching rockets using solid fuel.
Here in Dallas Friday, the Secretary of the Air Force paid us a visit.
Southwest Central News.
News. Secretary of the Air Force Eugene Zuckert spoke Friday noon before an Armed Forces Day
luncheon at the Sheraton Dallas Hotel. Later at a press conference, we asked Secretary
Zuckert this question. Mr. Secretary, you said in your speech today that the purpose
of armament is to maintain the peace rather than to wage war, and yet the goal for all
Western nations is eventual disarmament. Is there any problem in reconciling these two

I don't see any problem. I think that disarmament, especially in view of the terrible nature of the weapons that we have developed, is a rational and desirable objective. But so long as arms do exist, it's important that we have the arms to protect ourselves and to deter.
At this point, Mr. Zuckert, the Air Force is pinning its national defense hopes on the Minuteman missile for one thing.
What's the status of this missile at this time?
The Minuteman missile is in development, and we are satisfied with its progress.
It's on schedule.
We think it's going to be a very fine weapon system.
A setback such as today when the test did not go successfully is what you have to expect in the development of a new weapon system.
Q In the last few months we, of course, had a change in the administration in Washington.
Do you anticipate any further changes in policies of national defense?
THE PRESIDENT.
I couldn't give you a specific answer.
I think that the changes in policy were indicated in my speech today to give a greater emphasis
to limited war, to provide greater mobility to our forces.
I think a broader spectrum of ability to deter and to fight limited war
has been a keynote of this administration's policy.
I think you will see this foundation built upon in the budgets to come.
Would you care to make a comment as to the relative strengths of the United States Air Force
as compared to the Air Force of the Soviet Union?
No, because I would be guessing.
What I would say, though, is that the United States Air Force,
particularly our Strategic Air Command,
is a tremendously powerful instrument,
fully capable of carrying out its job of deterring attack upon the United States.
Air Force Secretary Eugene Zuckert in Dallas Friday.

Braniff revealed this week that it was going to install a million-dollar jet simulator
at its operations and maintenance base at Love Field.
It will duplicate flight conditions for pilots and trainees
and is slated to be installed in August.
American Airlines said this week it will expand its Dallas jet service June 11.
According to Bradford S. Gibson, American's district sales manager,
the new plans include inauguration of the first Dallas, Tennessee service,
the beginning of Dallas-El Paso jet service,
the first Dallas-San Diego jet service,
the start of a daily Dallas-Austin jet round trip,
and the addition of a third daily jet to Chicago from Dallas.
Are flying saucers real?
Yes, says a Dallas expert on the subject.
He is William Daniel of 8036 Fall River Drive.
This is what he had to say on the matter to us earlier.
Mr. Daniel, how long have you been studying this phenomenon known as flying saucers or unidentified flying objects?
Since late 1948.
Do you have reason to believe there are such things?
I think there are too many reliable reports by people in occupations such as airline pilots, radar men,
and technical personnel at rocket and installations of technological development
where technological development is going on that indicate this.
Well, do you have any documents to support what you're saying?
I have a statement I received recently.
It's a copy of a statement that is signed by 21 scientists, American scientists,
scientists who have urged that the Air Force check the UFOs more thoroughly and that an
investigation be made of the Air Force procedure.
Who are some of these scientists?
One of them, Dr. Charles P. Olivier, an American professor of astronomy, University of Pennsylvania,
and he was the president of the American Meteor Society.
Another one is Dr. Frederick P. Cranston, physicist, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory,
University of New Mexico.
And there are, as I say, 21 others, or 20 others.
Have you ever seen an unidentified flying object that you know wasn't a weather balloon
or something like that?
I have seen a group of unidentified objects which were unexplainable to me in early 1954.
What did they look like?
They looked like a group of small circular lights or luminescent objects in a concave
formation, and they went from south to north across the sky at night in approximately 15
seconds.
And you're sure they weren't ducks or geese or something like that?
I'm fairly certain from the standpoint there was no illuminating sources which would indicate
and they moved and they were observed too far to reflect the lights that could have possibly done so.
And at that time or that night, there was no full moon or any moon at all at that point.
In a recent book by a Colonel Tacker of the Air Force,
he said that flying saucers as such were something that could be explained almost 99% of the time.
Apparently you don't agree with this.
Not exactly, no, from the standpoint that they can be explained,
want that the explanation is the correct one.
Q Well, how many of these explanations do you think are valid? For example, you don't
think all of these objects are something from outer space or another world, do you?
A Not nearly all of them, no. There are too many people who are taking advantage of the
subject by writing books of the contactee nature. There are other people who write books
based on their hypothesis of how the saucers are propelled,
and they use, they gobble the UFO incidents to prove their point.
You mentioned contactee. What does that mean?
Someone who is alleged to have contacted an individual from another planet.
Don't you think some of these people are just doing it for the sensationalism or the money?
A great many of them are doing it for the money, and the other percentages, I do not
think, that are doing it for money are doing it because they have to have an escape and
a way to get their names known to the general public.
It's possibly an ego complex there.
Well, if there are such things as unidentified flying objects, and certain people have seen
them, why hasn't the government talked to these people?
benefit of their experience?
Well, from the standpoint that a few years ago there was an investigation set up by a
leading aircraft company to investigate antigravity processes to where we might someday be able
to utilize the force of gravity to repel the Earth's gravity and to go into space, this
was offered as an explanation for the saucer propulsion as early as 1950.
And as I say, the investigation by this prominent company did not start until 1955.
So do you think the Air Force may be covering up something here?
It seems that the times that they take up projects which are somewhat related to something that saucers are said to have done,
the non-existent saucers are said to have done, has come up quite a number of times in the last few years.
Thank you very much, Mr. Daniel.
Thank you.
